key_insight: DeepFEAv2 extends transient finite element surrogate modeling to both structured and unstructured meshes by using mesh connectivity to predict node- and element-based outputs over time.
engineering_relevance: It offers a scalable way to accelerate high-fidelity mechanical simulations, making near-real-time analysis more practical for complex FE problems.
method: Builds an input sequence from the FE connectivity matrix and element-wise features.
Uses a neural architecture tailored for joint transient prediction of NEO outputs.
Adds an FEA-informed regularization strategy to improve physical consistency of predictions.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on structured and unstructured 3D linear elastic datasets plus a pressure-driven aortic valve case, achieving up to R²=0.99, normalized error as low as 0.38%, and inference up to three orders of magnitude faster than FEA.
watch_item: Performance may depend on accurate mesh connectivity and careful adaptation to different element types or unseen FE topologies.
paper_title: DeepFEAv2: Deep Learning for Transient Finite Element Analysis Beyond Structured Meshes
